segments.text: Review the system from the previous lecture and ask for a systematic algorithm that replaces geometric guessing.
Use one concrete matrix. First choose a pivot, then multiply the pivot row, and next subtract it from a lower row to eliminate an entry.
Write every elimination step beside the changing matrix and explain which equation operation it represents.
Show a wrong pivot case where elimination fails. Ask what caused the error and correct it by exchanging rows.
Check the result with back substitution. If the recovered variables do not satisfy the original equations, trace the first incorrect row operation.
Summarize the algorithm as elimination followed by back substitution, and transfer it to a new three-by-three system.
